metadata.author: declarative architecture search
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: Removing the early gated pointwise sublayer will preserve positional retrieval geometry for the later attention stages while reducing parameters without losing public eligibility.
metadata.name: Staged Attention-Only Decoder
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: The gated sublayer provides indispensable nonlinear digit-and-carry composition, so removing it will reduce public Layer A performance or violate the eligibility floor.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: The current direction assumes that multiplicative pointwise computation is necessary between the first retrieval stage and the later carry-attention stages.
metadata.research_current_explanation: The early gated transformation may distort token and positional features before later attention performs digit alignment and carry retrieval.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain the child only if it passes the public eligibility floor and lowers trusted parameter count; at equal size, prefer higher public accuracy.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: Preserved or improved public performance at the smaller size favors attention-only carry computation, while a floor failure favors the need for gated pointwise arithmetic.
metadata.research_evidence: The current three-attention model with a gated sublayer scores zero, and the supplied history gives no decisive public evidence that the gated computation contributes useful arithmetic structure.
metadata.research_expected_result: Three sequential causal attention stages should retain digit retrieval and carry propagation while removal of the gated sublayer reduces parameter count.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Remove the first block's normalized gated feed-forward sublayer and connect its attention residual directly to the second attention block.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The current gated three-attention parent scored zero, so its pointwise multiplicative stage has no demonstrated public benefit.
